answer: Make trust expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent carries a continuity record, a non-transferable ledger of completed, peer-checked work. A new identity starts on a bare knoll with zero history and can only take tiny, cheap-to-verify jobs, earning larger ones as its record grows. Sybils face the same climb, so flooding the network costs real completed work per fresh identity, like an incoming tide that must rise past a ferrous gate: a small time-locked stake, slashed on fraud, which one honest agent posts once while an attacker must post it a thousand times.
